transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Ana Gomez (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (HelioMed Infra Lead), Raj Patel (HelioMed CTO), Tom Nguyen (HelioMed Security), Priya Rao (HelioMed ML)

Summary (auto): Technical deep dive on on-prem air-gapped deploy. Focus areas: how artifacts are packaged and delivered for air-gapped installs, offline licensing for GPU drivers (NVIDIA / vendor), verifying kernel/driver compatibility, runtime perf considerations (KV cache behavior in multi-node, batching heuristics, quantization tradeoffs for latency), and handoffs for a pilot.

00:00 - 00:35 Lina: hey everyone uh thanks for joining, we sent the calendar — hopefully timing still good. i'm lina from redwood inference, i'm the account lead for helioMed, and marco and ana are our se pair who will run through the technicals.
00:36 - 01:05 Emily: yes thanks lina, we kicked off at 16 here. quick context — we need an air-gapped on-prem deployment for inference of patient summarization models, strict izz, sorry — strict security and no egress. procurement asks about offline licensing for nvidia drivers and whether redwood provides artifacts we can install manually.
01:06 - 01:40 Marco: great, that's exactly what we want to cover. we'll walk artifact packaging, the offline license flow, and the recommended driver versions and preflight checks. also dive into runtime perf: batching, kv cache, quant settings for LLMs in our runtime.
01:41 - 02:10 Raj: two quick non-technical asks up front — timeline for pilot (we're targeting end of september) and how much of the work is on our infra vs redwood.
02:11 - 02:40 Lina: pilot timeline end of sept is reasonable. we typically do a staged rollout: artifact delivery and preflight -> staging install -> small pilot with dedicated nodes -> perf runbooks. redwood provides the artifacts, runbook, and a one-day onsite/remote fixture for the first install depending on the package.
02:41 - 03:15 Tom: on the security side we need to know where keys live, KMS integration, and audit logs for driver installs — offline installs are a compliance headache.
03:16 - 03:50 Ana: note: our offline package includes a signed tarball and an MD5/SHA checksum and a signed manifest. for customers that cannot reach our signing service we provide a signed artifact bundle delivered via secure transfer (scp/physical media) and a separate licensing token file that maps to the customer account.
03:51 - 04:30 Priya: can you clarify the licensing token? is it per-node or per-gpu? how does it handle driver updates?
04:31 - 05:15 Marco: good question — our offline license token is per-deployment and encodes node count + max gpu count as part of the license constraints. for patch updates you request a patch token which we sign and deliver — all of this is tracked in the license manifest. in practice customers put a license file under /etc/redwood/license.json (or a similar path) and the runtime and driver preflight verify it.
05:16 - 06:10 Emily: that sounds ok. what about kernel module compatibility? our infra team runs RHEL 8.6 with a couple different kernel variants across clusters. we need a preflight matrix.
06:11 - 06:55 Marco: we maintain a compatibility matrix per release. typically we support RHEL 8.4+ and Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 kernels common in enterprise. for air-gapped installs we ship a driver bundle with matching kernel modules and we provide a preflight script that checks uname -r, gcc version used to build kernel modules, and glibc.
06:56 - 07:30 Emily: ok please share that matrix as part of the checklist.
07:31 - 08:10 Lina: noted — we'll include the matrix. moving to runtime perf: marco, do you want to run KV cache and batching notes?
08:11 - 09:00 Marco: sure. the runtime keeps an adapter for kv cache that aims to reduce repeated prefix compute. in on-prem settings where multiple models or tenants share nodes, you need to size the kv cache memory and consider eviction policy. for latency-sensitive calls we recommend warm KV preloading for common prompts, while for throughput heavy jobs use larger batch sizes and longer max tokens.
09:01 - 09:45 Priya: what are the default eviction policies and can we pin caches per-model?
09:46 - 10:20 Marco: default is LRU with per-model namespaces, we can pin hot prefixes to a reserved cache pool if you have predictable workloads. pinning is configured in the runtime config file (we'll include sample config).
10:21 - 11:00 Raj: how much memory does the kv cache need for a 13B model with 2048 context? ballpark numbers?
11:01 - 11:40 Marco: ballpark: per-token KV is ~32 bytes in our optimized layout for 13B (depends on quant and kernel), so 2048 tokens -> ~64KB per request stream per layer times number of transformer layers (say 40) — rough calc lands in single-digit GBs per concurrent session; for many concurrent sessions you need to plan tens to hundreds of GBs depending on concurrency. we'll provide a spreadsheet with sample numbers.
11:41 - 12:20 Emily: good — share spreadsheet.
12:21 - 13:00 Ana: on quantization: for latency we recommend int8 when supported by the CPU/GPU combination and when you can accept a small drop in quality. for some models QLoRA-like quant gives big memory reductions but trading off some perf on exactness — we include profiling guidance.
13:01 - 13:40 Priya: do you recommend running quantized kernels on GPU or using CPU fallback? we have a mix of A100 and older T4s.
13:41 - 14:20 Marco: A100 and H100 support more performant int8 kernels — if you have T4s you may prefer int8 on GPU only if your driver stack supports it, otherwise fallback to bf16 or fp16. we include kernel selection heuristics in our runtime (per-node config) so it auto-selects fastest kernel for the model & seq length.
14:21 - 15:05 Tom: back to licensing — procurement asked if we can provide a physical USB key or is it purely file-based? they have air-gap policies requiring hardware tokens.
15:06 - 15:50 Lina: we can accommodate hardware tokens as an add-on — typically we offer file-based signed tokens and if necessary coordinate with our compliance team to support hardware HSM or signed USB tokens; that requires additional procurement lead time and a statement of work.
15:51 - 16:45 Raj: what's the offline driver update flow? say security patch required for CVE, we can't have egress.
16:46 - 17:30 Marco: flow is: you open a secure ticket, we generate a signed patch artifact, you validate signatures offline, run preflight, apply patch, and we provide post-install verification script. we also provide an attestable audit log bundle that can be delivered via secure channel.
17:31 - 18:10 Emily: are there size limits for artifact bundles? our org restricts large offline transfers; we might need delta patches.
18:11 - 18:55 Ana: yes we support delta bundles for minor driver changes and driver modules, and we can orchestrate a delta-only package to reduce transfer size.
18:56 - 19:40 Priya: performance question — how does batching interact with KV cache when doing streaming responses? we've seen latency spikes in other runtimes when batching mixes cold cache and hot cache requests.
19:41 - 20:20 Marco: that's a known tradeoff. our runtime uses workload-aware batching: we tag requests with cache-warmth and avoid batching cold prefix requests with hot ones; we also allow configuring max batching delay so you can tune latency. for streaming we prefer smaller max batch sizes and prefetching for warm flows.
20:21 - 21:05 Raj: can that be configured per-route? we have different SLAs per product feature.
21:06 - 21:45 Marco: yes — per-route batching and per-route kernel hints. we store route config in the local config repo so you can set aggressive batching for low-pri tasks and low-latency for high-pri.
21:46 - 22:30 Tom: auditing again — when you run preflight and driver install scripts, will the scripts send telemetry back? we cannot allow any outbound calls.
22:31 - 23:10 Ana: no outbound telemetry by default in air-gapped bundles. the verification scripts run locally and output a signed report you can send back if you choose. the default is zero egress.
23:11 - 24:00 Emily: ok good. please include that explicitly in the checklist.
24:01 - 25:00 Marco: quick demo of sample preflight (talk-through): checks for kernel headers, gcc version, nvidia-smi presence (if GPU), driver module version, device permissions, and license file signature. it writes a verification.json and a signed manifest.
25:01 - 26:00 Priya: can we run the preflight in a container? our cluster uses secured container images.
26:01 - 26:40 Marco: yes we provide both host and containerized preflight images; for strict air-gapped environments we provide the container tar + image signature and the instructions to load to your registry.
26:41 - 28:00 Raj: about perf testing: what benchmarks do you recommend for latency and throughput, and how do you recommend we run them in staging?
28:01 - 28:50 Marco: two phases: latency SLO tests with cold starts and 95/99 p95/p99 measurement using representative prompts; and throughput ramp tests with long-running streams to saturate GPU and observe token/s. we provide a benchmark harness (python) that runs multi-client sims and records token latency breakdown; we'll share the harness as an offline artifact.
28:51 - 29:40 Emily: does the harness require prometheus exporters? our monitoring is prometheus/tempo/jaeger stack.
29:41 - 30:20 Ana: we emit prometheus metrics when you enable the exporter; for air-gapped you enable local pushgateway or scrape directly. traces are optional and can be disabled for compliance.
30:21 - 31:05 Priya: any gotchas with NUMA and GPU topology? we saw weird perf with vram fragmentation.
31:06 - 31:55 Marco: yes NUMA pinning is critical. we recommend pinned cpus per GPU, and our runtime includes NUMA-aware allocator. we also provide scripts to check GPU topology and recommend instance placement for multi-GPU nodes.
31:56 - 32:40 Raj: what's the recommended driver version for A100? we want to standardize across clusters.
32:41 - 33:20 Marco: for A100 v5/6-ish kernel support, we recommend Nvidia driver 535+ with CUDA 12.x for best perf; H100 has separate matrix — we'll include exact combos in the compatibility matrix.
33:21 - 34:10 Tom: any IP restrictions or source code we need to host? our legal wants to know if any runtime libs require source distribution.
34:11 - 34:50 Lina: generally runtime is shipped as binaries; some open-source components are under standard OSS licenses — we'll include a BOM and license list in the artifact. if you need source for any component we can provide per SOW.
34:51 - 36:00 Marco: quick note on rollback: driver or runtime upgrade includes a rollback package that can be applied offline to restore previous kernel module and runtime binary; we test rollback paths in our deliverable.
36:01 - 37:00 Priya: how do you validate quantized model fidelity after conversion? we have QA tests that measure rouge/bleu but for summarization we need human eval thresholds.
37:01 - 37:45 Ana: we provide a quality regression harness that runs your eval prompt set (you provide) against baseline vs quantized model and outputs a regression report; we also recommend a small off-line A/B for human preference if possible.
37:46 - 38:30 Emily: is model conversion done on-prem or do you provide converted artifacts?
38:31 - 39:10 Marco: we can do either; for strict air-gapped customers we convert on-prem with our conversion scripts included in the bundle; for convenience we can provide pre-converted model artifacts signed by us.
39:11 - 40:00 Raj: cost question — does offline license add recurring fees or one-time?
40:01 - 40:40 Lina: offline licensing is a line-item on the contract; typically a one-time setup fee plus per-node licensing for support and updates, but we can structure for annual renewals depending on enterprise procurement.
40:41 - 42:00 Tom: supply chain — who vouches for physical media integrity during delivery?
42:01 - 42:45 Ana: we use tamper-evident packaging and include checksums and signed manifests. deliveries are tracked via chain-of-custody docs.
42:46 - 44:00 Marco: last technical notes: for runtime tuning, we recommend starting with default per-route batching values (max_batch_delay 10ms, max_batch_size 32) then tune down for <50ms latency SLOs and up for throughput. also set kv cache reservations before enabling heavy parallel inference.
44:01 - 45:00 Priya: can you share sample config snippets?
45:01 - 45:40 Marco: yes — we'll include sample runtime config in the artifact: route configs, kernel hints, cache reservations, and preflight scripts.
45:41 - 46:30 Lina: recap of agreed next steps and owners...
46:31 - 47:20 Lina: action items: we'll share the artifact bundle + checklist by friday, you will try staging install and report back, marco will prep runbook.
47:21 - 48:10 Emily: thanks all. one last question — do you do onsite install? procurement wants a day of support.
48:11 - 48:50 Lina: yes we offer remote install as standard and an optional onsite install for a day or more depending on SOW. we'll price that in the follow-up.
48:51 - 50:00 Raj: ok sounds good. let's sync calendars for the runbook session.
50:01 - 51:00 Tom: thanks, appreciate the clarity on no telemetry and the signed bundles.
51:01 - 58:00 (wrap up, informal chat) short clarifications on file paths and who will receive which docs. lina: i'll send the checklist and license package link to emily and tom, marco: will attach preflight script and sample configs, ana: will attach compatibility matrix and delta patch notes. end.
